hypothesis: If spider thread comes off the body surface like bark and not from an internal excretion, a public anatomical table will code the silk material of spiders as a surface slough and not as secretion from internal silk glands through spinnerets.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. The claim is supported only if a retrieved file codes the origin of the silk thread for at least five spider species and every one of those species is coded as surface slough, bark-like shedding or an external secretion with no internal silk gland.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. The claim is refuted if at least five spider species are coded and at least one is coded as producing silk in an internal gland that opens through a spinneret or spigot. If the only public files in the planned deposit are image stacks or scanner-settings notes, with no species-by-origin table, the verdict is inconclusive with reason data-unavailable. Image stacks larger than 5 MB are not downloaded and are not treated as a measurement.
interpretation: Aristotle denies Democritus: the thread is not a superfluity from inside the animal but comes off the body like bark, and spiders can spin from birth. This test scores only the origin of the thread, internal gland versus surface slough. Age at first spinning is not in the planned deposit and is not scored. Spinneret muscles and spigots are the exit; they refute the bark reading only when the same source codes the silk as coming from an internal gland.

test_contract.expected_observation: A species-level coding in which spider silk is a surface slough and internal silk glands are absent, for at least five species.
test_contract.disconfirming_observation: A coding, for at least one of five or more species, that silk is secreted by an internal gland and leaves through a spinneret.
test_contract.admissible_datasets: A public table or equally explicit coding of silk origin, not an unsegmented microCT stack and not a scanner-settings sheet. The deposit has to be retrievable without a login.
test_contract.inference_method: Read the CKAN package manifest. Download only resources under 200 KB. Accept a file only if its text codes silk origin for named species. Otherwise data-unavailable. No image measurement is attempted.

caveats: The CKAN package manifest was read before registration: 38 ZIP resources and one PDF, CT-Settings.pdf, of about 139 KB. The ZIPs are microCT stacks. Their voxel values were not downloaded. The PDF was not downloaded.
A stack could in principle be segmented to locate glands. That analysis is not this test. Absence of a coded table is data-unavailable, not evidence for Aristotle or for Democritus.

datasets.name: Anatomical atlas of the spider spinneret muscle system
datasets.role: public deposit checked for a table of silk origin; image stacks were not measured

method: Read the CKAN package manifest and hashed it. Resources of 200 KB or more were not downloaded; the ZIP resources are microCT stacks above 5 MB. The one resource under 200 KB was downloaded, hashed, and its text extracted. It was accepted as a measurement only if it coded silk origin for at least five species. It did not, so the pre-registered data-unavailable rule applies.
results_summary: The deposit lists 39 resources, of which 38 are ZIP image stacks and 1 is under 200 KB. The small file does not code silk as an internal gland versus a surface slough for five species.
